From cod. Laur. 28, 34 (A) f. 58v and Laur. 28, 13 (B) f. 143r transcribed and collated
by Wuensch; with B it agrees so much, that it seems to have been transcribed from it, Marc. 335, f. 336r,
which Kroll inspected. 1 τοῦ αὐτοῦ θ. etc. ('of the same Th. etc.') thus A, θ. περὶ καταρχῶν ('Th. on inceptions') B.

1 De Theophilo, Thomae filio, Edesseno, homine perinde graecae atque syriacae
linguae perito, propter astrologiae scientiam Chaliphae Almahdio acceptissimo,
Bagdadae ann. 785 p. C. n. mortuo, cf. Wenrich, De auctorum graecorum versioni-
bus, 1842, pp. 14, 73 ; Whright, Syriac Literature, 1894, p. 163 sqq. et supra, p. 83,
n. 4. — De operibus Theophili copiosius in catalogo Parisino disputabimus. Vide
codd. Paris. 2417, f. 4v s.; 2506, f. 108 ss. et cf. cod. Vatican. 212, f. 205 ss.; cod.
Angelican. 29, f. 275 ss.
sections.en:
1 On Theophilus, son of Thomas, of Edessa, a man equally skilled in the Greek and Syriac
languages, most acceptable to the Caliph Al-Mahdi on account of his knowledge of astrology,
who died at Baghdad in the year 785 A.D., cf. Wenrich, De auctorum graecorum versioni-
bus, 1842, pp. 14, 73 ; Wright, Syriac Literature, 1894, p. 163 sqq. and above, p. 83,
n. 4. — On the works of Theophilus we shall discuss more fully in the Parisian catalogue. See
codd. Paris. 2417, f. 4v s.; 2506, f. 108 ss. and cf. cod. Vatican. 212, f. 205 ss.; cod.
Angelican. 29, f. 275 ss.

summary.headline: Theophilus on Cosmic Inceptions
summary.text: Astrological method for determining the horoscoping sign and planetary rulers through ordered hours, cosmic transits, local configurations, and a worked conjunction-in-Cancer example. Theophilus’ collection then begins its discussion of the Egyptian year’s start at the rising of the Dog Star, using lunar epochs and stellar positions.
